Impeccable 3.7 brings linting to design.

Until now it was a skill you asked for help. Now it's a design-system-aware feedback loop that runs while your agent builds, catching slop and design drift before they land.

🪝 Design hooks for Claude, Codex, and Cursor
They run after every UI edit and quietly nudge your agent to fix slop and drift. The output isn't another wall of lint: it separates new findings from already-seen ones, flags clean scans, and asks the agent to use judgment. Fix real issues, leave intentional demos alone, save exceptions to config instead of littering your source.

🎨 Slop detection is now project-aware
Reads your actual design system from DESIGN.md, your typography, palette, radius scale, and tokens, and flags drift from your system, not just generic AI slop:
• this font isn't in your design system
• this color is outside your documented palette
• this radius doesn't match your rounded scale
The same engine powers both the hooks and the CLI, and it's where we're investing next.

🖥️ Live Mode, ready for real projects
Svelte/SvelteKit now preview variants as temporary framework components with live params, then accept cleanly back into your source component. Manual text edits got evidence / apply / discard routes, insertions preserve their anchors, and mapped lists and JSX slots clean up far more reliably.

⚡ Leaner core, sharper detector
Rule-level evals across 3 providers and 4 niches cut guidance with no measurable lift and dropped examples that taught models bad patterns. The detector now skips hidden and screen-reader-only elements, understands OKLCH alpha and Sass-like inputs, and tightened checks for repeated kickers, oversized H1s, clipped overflow, and cramped padding.

🛠️ CLI caught up
impeccable detect loads DESIGN.md by default, motion findings name the exact token or cubic-bezier instead of just "bounce," and impeccable ignores gives real CRUD for exceptions. Hooks and CLI share the same ignores. No split-brain config. Plus a much-improved interactive installer with hooks setup built in.

Upgrade:
npx impeccable install
npm i -g impeccable

content:
The next major consumer crypto product isn’t another L2, perp DEX or AI agent.

It’s crypto cards.

For years, crypto payments promised to bridge Web2 and Web3, but adoption remained limited. Most products were little more than prepaid cards that converted crypto into fiat at the point of sale.

That has changed.

According to @DefiLlama, crypto card issuers are now processing hundreds of millions of dollars in monthly payment volume, with billions of dollars in cumulative spending. More importantly, growth is no longer concentrated in a single provider. An entire ecosystem is beginning to emerge.

——

At first glance, every crypto card looks the same.

You load your wallet, tap your Visa or Mastercard, earn cashback and go about your day.

Under the hood, they’re built on completely different assumptions.

Three models are beginning to emerge.

——

● Exchange Cards

Platforms like @coinbase , @binance , https://t.co/eXZmTmqnJm and @Bybit_Official already own one of the hardest things to acquire in finance: users.

Their advantage isn’t the card itself it’s distribution.

• Trading, custody and payments all live within the same ecosystem

• The card extends products users already rely on

• The moat is customer ownership, not cashback

——

● Stablecoin Banks

Projects like @KASTxyz, @RedotPay and @Plasma are betting that stablecoins become the primary financial account for millions of people.

Instead of asking users to top up a spending wallet, they want salaries, savings, transfers and everyday payments to happen entirely on-chain.

The card isn’t the product.

It’s the interface.

• Stablecoin-native banking

• Global payments

• Savings, transfers and spending in one experience

• Strong opportunity across emerging markets

——

● Self-Custody Spending

Projects like @ether_fi, @gnosispay and @useTria are taking a different approach.

Rather than forcing users to sell productive assets every time they spend, they’re building systems that preserve ownership while unlocking liquidity.

• Spend against productive assets

• Maintain self-custody

• Preserve capital efficiency

• Abstract blockchain complexity

——

The interesting part isn’t which company ranks #1 today.

It’s that every team is solving the same problem from a different direction.

• Exchange cards compete on distribution.

• Stablecoin banks compete to become your primary financial account.

• Self-custody cards compete on ownership and capital efficiency.

The competition isn’t about offering the highest cashback.

It’s about becoming the default interface between users and on-chain finance.

——

For years, the industry believed mass adoption would happen when millions of people learned how to use DeFi.

What if the opposite is true?

What if DeFi reaches billions of users by disappearing into products they already understand?

Nobody thinks about payment rails when tapping a bank card.

Nobody thinks about cloud infrastructure when opening an app.

The infrastructure disappears.

Only the experience remains.

Crypto is beginning to follow the same path.

The biggest winners won’t necessarily be the protocols with the best technology.

They’ll be the products that make blockchain invisible.

AI初心者が仕事を全部AIでやる。は無理で、

理由は最適な安定するモデル選んで、ディレクトリミリ単位でイジって、使ってる全SaaSとAIをAPI繋いで、

各タスクに必要なコンテキストを考えてからAIに参照させて、テスト出力して、確認、レビュー、改善をloopさせて、その後実際に現場で結果出るか確認して、その後skill化して、

毎回同じような出力にならないようにルールを守らせた上でランダム性が出るようにskill調節して、良いskillになったら定期自動実行設定する。

ということをしなきゃいけない。鬼大変。IQと時間と言語化力とAIスキルが全部必要。

そしてそもそも「対人」の営業やフロント対応はまだ無理だし、細かくいうとリアルの動き、ロボティクスの領域は全然ダメ。

もちろんゆくゆくは未来でAIが推論も正確。文字、画像、動画を素早く最適に処理できるように進化しきったら、さらにできることは増えるだろうけど、

そうなっても結局、個人や法人しか持ってない情報を取り込むということはどんなにAIが進化しても必須。

ガチでAIの無限リソースをフルに使って結果を出すなら、AIにランダム性と独自性を持たせた出力をさせるのが必須。

だからそのプロセス設計して個人の一次情報を楽に素早く全部データに変換し続けるフローを設計する必要がある。

それをしないでAI使ってる人は誰でも出せる価値のないものを出力してる人か、そもそも誰でもできる仕事をしてる人。これのどちらか。

We were flying at an extremely, extremely low altitude.

content:
Iranian F-5 pilot who bombed US Buehring base in Kuwait:

We were flying at an extremely, extremely low altitude.

From a flight-standard perspective, the standard training altitude is around 500 feet, but we were below 50 feet.

We knew that Patriot systems were deployed in the area, and that this base had multi-layered air defense. Given Kuwait’s cooperation, they were protecting this base, and scrambled F-18s were monitoring it.

Even though we knew AWACS aircraft were up there and surveillance/listening sites were active, the entire flight was conducted under complete radio silence.

I should mention here that there were 2-3 ships, we were flying so low that we passed between 2 ships, and their decks were higher than us. In other words, the sailors were looking down at us from the deck.

We passed through there, and thank God, entered Kuwaiti waters, and from there entered Kuwait itself.

When we entered Kuwait, the high-voltage power lines suddenly became 10x times more numerous. Their refineries and forces were along our route, all of them were within our reach. 

We could have bombed them immediately without any problem. But our target was Camp Buehring.

We carried out this route at very high speed and very low altitude. And then, when we reached the base, we bombed it successfully.

生前に首を吊った場合（自殺など）と、死後に偽装として首を吊られた場合（他殺の隠蔽など）では、遺体にはっきりと異なる特徴や違和感が残ります。その主な違いは以下の通りです。

content:
自殺と他殺（死後縊死：死んだ後に首を吊られた状態）を見分けることは、法医学や検視において非常に重要なテーマであり、明確な判断基準が存在します。

生前に首を吊った場合（自殺など）と、死後に偽装として首を吊られた場合（他殺の隠蔽など）では、遺体にはっきりと異なる特徴や違和感が残ります。その主な違いは以下の通りです。

1. 索条痕（さくじょうこん：ロープの跡）の違和感
首に残るロープの跡は、生前か死後かを見分ける最大のポイントの一つです。

生活反応（生前の証拠）の有無:生きてる状態で首を吊ると、ロープが皮膚に擦れたり圧迫されたりすることで、皮膚の剥離（擦過傷）や、その周囲に皮下出血（内出血）が起こります。また、擦れた部分が乾燥して茶褐色に変色する「革皮様化（かくひようか）」という現象が起きます。
死後の偽装の場合:すでに心臓が止まって血流がない状態（死後）でロープをかけられても、強い内出血（生活反応）は起こりません。ロープの形に皮膚が凹むことはありますが、生前のような鮮やかな赤紫色の内出血や、生体ならではの組織の変化は見られません。

2. 吉川線（よしかわせん）の有無
激しい抵抗の跡:もし被害者が首を絞められて殺害された（扼殺や絞殺）あとに、自殺に見せかけるために吊るされた場合、被害者は首を絞められている最中に必死に抵抗します。その際、自分の首にかけられた紐や手を引きはがそうとして、自分の爪で自分の首の皮膚を掻きむしった跡（吉川線）が残ることがよくあります。

自殺の場合:自ら首を吊る場合は、通常このような自己を傷つける激しい掻き傷は残りません。
3. 死斑（しはん）の位置と移動
人間は死亡すると、重力に従って血液が体の低い方に沈殿し、皮膚に赤紫色の「死斑」が現れます。

自殺（立った状態で吊り下がった場合）:血液が下半身や手先に沈むため、両手の下半分や、両足の膝から下に濃い死斑（下垂体死斑）が現れます。
他殺・偽装の場合:もし一度ベッドや床の上などで仰向けの状態で死亡（あるいは殺害）し、一定時間が経ってからロープで吊るされた場合、死斑は最初に横たわっていた「背中側」に強く形成されます。死後しばらく経つと、体位を変えても死斑は完全には移動しないため、「首を吊っているのに、なぜか背中に強い死斑がある」という決定的な違和感（死斑の矛盾）が生じます。

4. 骨折や内部組織の損傷の違い
生前（高い位置からのドロップなど）:突発的に強い衝撃が加わって首を吊った場合、首の骨（頚椎）の骨折や、喉の軟骨（舌骨や甲状軟骨）の骨折、筋肉の断裂が起こることがあります。この際、周囲の組織には強い内出血を伴います。

死後の偽装:死後に遺体を吊り上げた場合、骨が折れることはあっても、やはりその周囲に「血流があったことによる内出血（浸潤）」が起きないため、解剖によって生前のものか死後のものかが判別できます。
5. 周辺環境や着衣の矛盾

体そのものだけでなく、現場の状況にも違和感が現れます。
靴底や足の汚れ:台に上って自ら吊ったのであれば、台の上の足跡や靴の擦れ跡が残ります。しかし、意識がない状態や死体を持ち上げて吊るした場合、不自然に衣服が乱れたり、周囲の家具が不自然に動いていたり、あるいは足を乗せるべき台が存在しない・位置が遠すぎるなどの矛盾が生じます。

法医学の現場では、これらの視覚的な特徴に加え、顕微鏡を使った組織検査や血液検査、薬物検査などを組み合わせることで、それが本当に自発的なものか、あるいは他者の手が加わったものかを科学的に厳密に特定しています。

つまりこの５つの自殺or他殺のラインをわずかな期間で判断し、断定した茨城県警

ってことだよね

title: Under-16 social media ban announced by UK government
content: The UK is the latest country to follow Australia in implementing a total social media ban for children under 16, Prime Minister Keir Starmer has announced. The ban, which could take effect from early next year, will be joined by wider measures that will also prevent children from talking to strangers in online games, livestreaming, or using sexual or romantic chatbots. "Do we truly believe that social media creates a happy environment for our children? Do we truly believe that it's a place where they can feel safe?" title: The Free and Open Web Is Under Attack at the IETF
content: The ability to access publicly available information using automated tools is a central value and benefit of a free and open internet. Automated access—often called crawling or scraping—powers important, useful tools for locating, preserving, and analyzing online information. For example, crawling and scraping helps journalists, researchers, and watchdog organizations report the news, find security flaws, and investigate discrimination. Crawling the web allows non-profits like the Internet Archive to preserve historical copies of websites. Tools for automated comparison shopping allow consumers to find the best deals on items they want to buy. And so on. Yet the open internet access is increasingly under threat from publishers and Big Tech companies alike. Fearing lost advertising and licensing revenues, website operators increasingly claim that they need to lock down their sites from bots that crawl public web content to train or operate AI models. Some companies are even trying to embed their business models into internet standards by changing Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) technical standards that shape much of the internet. Many of their economic anxieties are understandable. AI bots can strain websites’ infrastructure, in some cases, degrading site performance or taking them offline altogether. Upgrading systems costs money that some sites may not have. And AI is likely to disrupt the business models many publishers adopted in response to the rise of the internet, if users rely on AI overviews instead of visiting source websites. However reasonable these fears may be, the answer is not to chang e the IETF standards from neutral protocols that encourage openness to restrictive requirements designed to monetize internet access. The worst of these proposed standards would give websites far greater ability to automatically block legitimate, lawful scraping and crawling. title: The NO FAKES Act Could Silence Satire, Commentary, And News
content: The NO FAKES Act is supposed to target harmful AI-generated impersonations. But in reality, it will make it easier to suppress commentary, satire, and other lawful speech. That's why EFF has signed a letter urging the Senate Judiciary Committee not to advance the bill in its current form. Take action Tell Congress to Say No to NO FAKES In the letter, EFF joins a coalition of civil society groups in pointing out that the bill would import many of the worst features of the DMCA notice-and-takedown system into an even broader range of online expression. Faced with a “heckler’s veto” over legal speech, platforms will have incentives to remove content first and ask questions later. The bill offers no protection for a platform’s judgment about an often difficult question—whether a particular piece of content is satire, parody, commentary, or news. Any platform that guesses wrong faces penalties of up to $750,000 per work. NO FAKES could also undermine the rights of the people it is supposed to protect. The new federal “likeness” right could be licensed or transferred to others, so individuals will lose control over the use of their own face and voice. That’s not theoretical—workers in the entertainment industry are routinely asked to sign broad contracts about the future use of their likenesses. As the letter notes: A background actor who signs a release on set or an ordinary person who clicks through a platform's terms of service could end up with the right to their own face and voice in someone else's hands, for years, with federal enforcement behind it. EFF and the other signatories urge Congress to examine existing legal remedies and pursue narrowly tailored solutions to genuine harms. The last thing we need is a sweeping new intellectual property right that threatens free expression.
